findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the reference: the content-type filter to widen for STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT lives in `corpus._load_ticket_events` (`_CONTENT_TYPES`, both the batch-cat sha selection at corpus.py:134 and the read gate at :139), not in `_enumerate_event_blobs` (which enumerates all blobs).
evidence: Plan: 'extending `corpus._enumerate_event_blobs`'s content-type filter to also recover STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT blobs'
corpus.py:69-88 `_enumerate_event_blobs` returns every blob matching the path regex with no TYPE filter
corpus.py:130-140 `_load_ticket_events` is where `if b.kind in _CONTENT_TYPES` / `if b.kind not in _CONTENT_TYPES` gating happens
findings.finding: The plan attributes the CONTENT-TYPE filter to `corpus._enumerate_event_blobs`, but that function applies no content-type filter — it enumerates ALL event blobs; the `_CONTENT_TYPES` filter (`CREATE/EDIT/FILE_IMPACT/REVIEW_RESULT`) lives in `corpus._load_ticket_events` (corpus.py:134,139).
findings.location: Approach → 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, via env override)'
scenarios: An implementer following the plan literally edits `_enumerate_event_blobs` looking for a content-type gate that isn't there, and misses that the read-side filter (and the batch-cat sha selection at corpus.py:134) is what must actually be widened to recover STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT bodies.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'mirroring `corpus._load_ticket_events`'s `_CONTENT_TYPES` read gate, widened to STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT (extending both the batch-cat sha selection and the body-parse gate)'.

findings.checklist_item: Correct the ticket-level-walk description: state that _enumerate_event_blobs already returns all blob TYPEs and the content-type filter to widen (to include STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT) is _load_ticket_events/_CONTENT_TYPES — and say explicitly whether labels.py reimplements the body read or edits corpus.py (adding corpus.py to Scope if so).
evidence: corpus.py:69 `def _enumerate_event_blobs(tracker_path)` returns a `_Blob` for EVERY path matching `_PATH_RE`, with no kind filter
corpus.py:134 the content-type filter lives in `_load_ticket_events`: `content_shas = [b.sha for b in blobs if b.kind in _CONTENT_TYPES]`
corpus.py:36 `_CONTENT_TYPES = {"CREATE", "EDIT", "FILE_IMPACT", "REVIEW_RESULT"}` — the module constant that would need widening if the filter were extended there
findings.finding: The plan attributes the content-type filter to the wrong corpus symbol: it says the ticket-level walk works by 'extending corpus._enumerate_event_blobs's content-type filter to also recover STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT blobs', but _enumerate_event_blobs (corpus.py:69) applies no content-type filter at all — it returns every event blob (all TYPEs) deduped by (ticket_id, uuid). The _CONTENT_TYPES restriction ({CREATE, EDIT, FILE_IMPACT, REVIEW_RESULT}) is applied one layer up in _load_ticket_events (corpus.py:134: content_shas = [b.sha for b in blobs if b.kind in _CONTENT_TYPES]). So there is nothing to 'extend' on _enumerate_event_blobs; the STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT bodies must be selected and cat'd by labels.py's own logic (calling _enumerate_event_blobs + _batch_cat) or by changing _load_ticket_events/_CONTENT_TYPES.
findings.location: Approach → 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, via env override)'
scenarios: Implementer follows the plan literally and looks for a content-type filter inside _enumerate_event_blobs, finds none, and is unsure whether corpus.py must be modified
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'labels.py calls corpus._enumerate_event_blobs (which already enumerates all blob TYPEs) then corpus._batch_cat, applying its OWN body-content filter for STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT — corpus._CONTENT_TYPES / _load_ticket_events are unchanged and corpus.py is not edited.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the jq proving command to the corpus's cache-listed (verified) ticket population (e.g. filter jq to the ticket_ids in labels-<hash>.jsonl) so the report count and the jq count compare the same population.
evidence: Plan: 'Read cache_dir / f"{content_hash}.jsonl" ... to get the corpus's ticket population ... this is the single driver for every downstream label; unverified rows never enter labels at all'
Plan: escaped_defect/reopen are computed only 'for that store's cache-listed ticket ids'
AC: 'the labels report counts matching independent jq counts over the store for plan_defect, caused_by and reopen events'
A store-wide jq count is a superset of the verified, cache-listed population, so equality is not expected.
findings.finding: The acceptance criterion validates label counts against 'independent jq counts over the store', but labels are scoped to the VERIFIED corpus ticket population only, whereas a jq count over the whole store includes tickets/events outside that population — the two counts will not match by construction.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, first checkbox: 'checked by the labels report counts matching independent jq counts over the store for plan_defect, caused_by and reopen events'
scenarios: The store contains plan_defect closes on tickets whose review sidecars were unverified or absent from the cache; the jq count exceeds the labels count and the AC 'fails' on a correct implementation.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the jq check is run over ONLY the (store, ticket_id) pairs present in the labels/cache file — e.g. pipe the cache ticket-id set into the jq filter — rather than an unscoped store-wide count.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the grouping and ordering that define 'consecutive reviews' (e.g. group by (store, ticket_id), order by review_event_ts, pair adjacent reviews).
evidence: Plan: 'for consecutive reviews (verified, surfaced findings only) with changed material, join by norm_id'
No stated grouping key (per ticket_id?) or ordering key (review_event_ts?) for what makes two reviews 'consecutive'.
'identical-material pairs' likewise depends on an unstated pairing/ordering rule.
findings.finding: The finding-level labels (resolved_by_author / persisted / noise_flip) operate on 'consecutive reviews', but the plan never states how reviews are grouped and ordered into the sequence that defines 'consecutive' — presumably per ticket ordered by review_event_ts, but this is left implicit.
scenarios: A ticket with three reviews R1<R2<R3: which pairs are compared (R1-R2, R2-R3, or R1-R3)? An executor could choose differently, producing different noise-flip and churn counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Reviews are grouped by (store, ticket_id) and ordered ascending by review_event_ts; a consecutive pair is any two temporally adjacent reviews for the same ticket.'

No plan text specifies whether a show_ticket failure for a verified cache-listed ticket is skipped, defaulted, or fatal

findings.location: Approach → 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, via env override)' bullet
scenarios: A store root present at corpus-build time is missing/re-pathed at labels-build time; show_ticket fails for every ticket in that store

evidence: Plan: 'reopen_count/force_close/completion_verifier_fail_count are REIMPLEMENTED directly in labels.py ... mirroring mine_outcome_corpus.py's definitions exactly'
mine_outcome_corpus.py:216-221 completion_verifier_fail_count filters on data.get('schema') == 'completion_verifier_fail_v1'
Plan: completion_failed_after_pass requires 'a recovered COMPLETION_VERDICT event for X with data.verdict == "FAIL"'

findings.finding: The reimplemented completion-verifier-fail helper is said to mirror mine_outcome_corpus.py 'exactly', but that script keys on data.schema=='completion_verifier_fail_v1' while the plan's own completion_failed_after_pass keys on a COMPLETION_VERDICT with data.verdict=='FAIL' — two different discriminators for the same event, with no statement of which the reimplemented helper uses.

findings.suggested_fix: Adopt schema=='completion_verifier_fail_v1' as the FAIL discriminator for both the reimplemented helper (matching mine_outcome_corpus.py) and completion_failed_after_pass, since it uniquely identifies FAIL records and excludes gate_error_v1/PASS records by construction.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify at which layer the UNVERIFIED-row exclusion is tested (in the verified-only cache read by labels.py, or a defense-in-depth re-check) so the synthetic corpus test targets labels.py's own behavior.
evidence: Context: 'writes cache_dir / ... one JSON line per VERIFIED row ONLY (_write_cache skips verified=False)'
Approach: 'Read cache_dir / f"{content_hash}.jsonl" (the SAME cache file, already VERIFIED-only)'
Testing: 'an UNVERIFIED corpus row never reaches any label'
findings.finding: The Testing section asserts 'an UNVERIFIED corpus row never reaches any label', but the label pipeline reads only the verified-only cache file (Context: '_write_cache skips verified=False'), so an unverified row can never appear in the cache that labels.py consumes — the test either duplicates a guarantee owned by corpus.py or must inject at a layer the plan does not describe.
findings.location: Testing section vs Context/Approach ('the SAME cache file, already VERIFIED-only')
scenarios: Test author writes a synthetic cache jsonl including a verified=False row to exercise exclusion, but labels.py never emits such rows into the cache — the exclusion happens in corpus.py, not in labels.py, so the test proves the wrong module.
findings.suggested_fix: Either have labels.py re-assert verified==True on each cache row it reads (and test that assertion), or state that the exclusion is inherited from corpus's verified-only cache and the test seeds the cache with a verified=False line to confirm labels.py skips it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the per-store tracker-dir selection is made concurrency-safe (pass tracker_git_root explicitly to show_ticket instead of mutating os.environ, or serialize/scope the walk) so the global env override cannot race a concurrent reader.
evidence: Plan: 'temporarily set os.environ["REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"] = tracker_git_root (restored in finally) around show_ticket(...)'
Context: 'config.tracker_dir_override() reads REBAR_TRACKER_DIR, winning verbatim over any config.'
T9 concurrency-safety: 'is shared/mutable state mutated atomically ... no check-then-act TOCTOU'
findings.finding: The plan mutates the process-global os.environ['REBAR_TRACKER_DIR'] around each per-store show_ticket call, but does not address concurrency/ownership safety of that global. os.environ is a shared, process-wide mutable state and config.tracker_dir_override() reads it 'verbatim over any config'; a temporary set/restore-in-finally window is a check-then-act TOCTOU on a global with no defined ownership or serialization.
findings.location: Approach → 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, via env override)'
scenarios: Any concurrent reader of tracker_dir_override() (e.g. another store's iteration, or a co-resident harness operation) during the mutation window observes the wrong store's tracker dir and reads the wrong ticket population.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer threading tracker_git_root through show_ticket as an explicit argument (avoiding the os.environ mutation entirely), or document that labels.py runs strictly single-threaded and serially per store.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Redirect per-store tracker reads without mutating the process-global REBAR_TRACKER_DIR (pass the tracker root explicitly), or state that labels.py is an offline batch tool never co-resident with a live MCP server.
evidence: Plan: 'temporarily set os.environ["REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"] = tracker_git_root (restored in finally)'
Context: 'config.tracker_dir_override() reads REBAR_TRACKER_DIR, winning verbatim over any config.'
Support matrix Harness cell: 'Python library, CLI, remote MCP'
findings.finding: The env-override mechanism assumes a process where mutating os.environ['REBAR_TRACKER_DIR'] is a safe, isolated way to redirect tracker reads. In the remote-MCP harness shape (a long-lived server), a per-store global env mutation is not isolated to the labels run and can affect co-resident harness operations that resolve their tracker dir via the same global.
findings.location: Approach → 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, via env override)'
scenarios: Harness = remote MCP server: while labels.py holds REBAR_TRACKER_DIR set to store A, a concurrent request resolving tracker_dir_override() reads store A's tracker dir instead of its own, returning tickets from the wrong tracker — an observable wrong result the MCP user witnesses.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass tracker_git_root directly to show_ticket / the store walk rather than round-tripping through os.environ.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the raw agreement / verdict-flip noise-floor metrics against chance-corrected inter-rater statistics (Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa or Krippendorff's alpha), or publish a chance-corrected figure alongside the raw pooled rate.
evidence: Plan: 'per-question Pass-2 agreement ... agreement = (matches)/(total compared), pooled across every finding/pair, published with its comparison count' and '(a) verdict flip rate'

Retrieved (galileo.ai, 2026): '“Raw agreement looks solid at 90%. But when you compute kappa, expected chance agreement is 0.905, making kappa approximately -0.05. The judge is doing nothing meaningful.”'
Retrieved (tagaroo.ai): 'raw percent agreement flatters your data, and kappa is the correction ... the one most often [asked for]'

Retrieved (cogn-iq.org): names the 'high-agreement-low-kappa paradox'; the arXiv IAA survey and datavlab LLM-evaluation guide both treat chance-corrected agreement as the norm for LLM-as-evaluator reliability

This is a novel measurement methodology (a published noise-floor that other consumers compare against), so the well-trodden-pattern ANTI-FP does not fully cover it — the plan picks the weaker of two established measures without saying why
findings.finding: The 'reviewer-noise floor' is an inter-rater reliability measurement, but the plan derives it from raw uncorrected statistics (pooled per-question agreement = matches/total, raw verdict-flip rate, Jaccard churn) with no consideration of the established chance-corrected agreement prior art (Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa, Krippendorff's alpha) that is standard-of-practice for exactly this problem.
findings.location: Approach → 'Noise floor' bullet; Acceptance Criteria bullet 2
scenarios: Two reviewers agreeing 90% on a PASS-skewed corpus report a strong noise floor, when chance-corrected agreement is near zero — the published floor is meaningless for the skewed criterion
A downstream replay consumer treats the raw agreement rate as a quality bar and accepts a candidate reviewer that is no better than chance
findings.suggested_fix: Publish a chance-corrected agreement statistic (Fleiss' kappa across the pooled pairs, or Krippendorff's alpha given the unbalanced pooling) next to the raw per-question agreement rate and verdict-flip rate, so a high raw rate driven by verdict prevalence is not mistaken for genuine reviewer stability.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State why escaped_defect/inbound caused_by may be read from show_ticket's compiled (compaction-folded) state while reopen/force_close/completion use the git-walk, and confirm the compiled state is compaction-safe for close_class + inbound caused_by (both survive SNAPSHOT folding) — or route all ticket-level signals through the single git-walk.
evidence: Plan: 'temporarily set os.environ["REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"] ... around show_ticket(ticket_id, include_inbound=True)' for escaped_defect/inbound_deps
Plan: 'reopen_count/force_close/completion_verifier_fail_count are REIMPLEMENTED ... fed from labels.py's own per-store git-walk'
mine_outcome_corpus.py docstring: '140 of 631 reviewed tickets (22%) have a SNAPSHOT but zero STATUS files on disk — so an on-disk scan would silently compute reopen_count=0'
findings.finding: The ticket-level labels draw from two independent recovery mechanisms with no stated consistency contract: show_ticket(include_inbound=True) reads COMPILED on-disk state (for close_class and inbound_deps caused_by), while reopen_count/force_close/completion_verifier_fail come from labels.py's own raw git-object walk. mine_outcome_corpus.py documents that on-disk state is compaction-lossy (22% of reviewed tickets have a SNAPSHOT but ZERO STATUS files on disk) — the exact reason it uses a git-walk. The plan does not justify why reopen/force_close/completion signals need the compaction-proof git-walk but escaped_defect/inbound caused_by can trust show_ticket's compiled state, nor whether the two sources may disagree.
findings.location: Approach — 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, via env override)' and 'Ticket-level labels'
scenarios: A compacted culprit ticket whose caused_by-inbound edge or close_class was folded into a SNAPSHOT is read one way by show_ticket but its STATUS/COMMENT history is read from git objects — a silent basis mismatch between escaped_defect and reopened for the same ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Since labels.py already performs a per-store git-walk recovering STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT, derive close_class (from the closing STATUS event's data.close_class) and inbound caused_by (from LINK events across the walk) from that same compaction-proof walk, dropping the show_ticket env-override path entirely — one source, no compiled/raw mismatch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the noise-floor bullet, acknowledge the e6_metrics.py / e6_judge_reliability.py prior art and state whether labels.py lifts those pure functions (jaccard/agreement) or reimplements them, with the reason for any divergence (norm_id-join granularity, per-question vs per-criterion unit).
evidence: Plan: 'over identical-material pairs: (a) verdict flip rate; (b) per-criterion churn (Jaccard by norm_id); (c) per-question Pass-2 agreement ... agreement = (matches)/(total compared), pooled across every finding/pair, published with its comparison count'
docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/e6_metrics.py:203 defines jaccard(a,b); lines 180-200 build a raw_agreement/kappa report dict

docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/e6_judge_reliability.py:636-660 already pools per-pair fired-criteria Jaccard and computes verdict agreement over identical-material (order-shuffle) permutations, publishing mean_fired_criteria_jaccard with its plan count

The plan explicitly names and mirrors the sibling harness mine_outcome_corpus.py for the ticket-level functions but says nothing about the noise-floor harnesses, though both are docs/experiments reference code
findings.finding: The noise-floor section reinvents agreement/Jaccard primitives that already exist as docs/experiments prior art (e6_metrics.py: jaccard/raw_agreement/fleiss_kappa/compute_agreement; e6_judge_reliability.py: pooled fired-criteria Jaccard + verdict agreement over identical-material permutations), without acknowledging that prior art or justifying reimplementation — an asymmetry versus the plan's explicit mirroring of mine_outcome_corpus.py's ticket-level functions.
scenarios: A reviewer/maintainer later discovers e6_metrics.jaccard and e6_judge_reliability's agreement logic and cannot tell whether labels.py intentionally diverged (e.g. norm_id join granularity, per-question vs per-criterion unit) or simply duplicated by omission
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence mirroring the mine_outcome_corpus.py treatment: name e6_metrics.jaccard / e6_judge_reliability's pooled-Jaccard-and-agreement as the reference, and note they are docs/experiments reference functions reimplemented (not imported) with the specific unit differences (finding-level norm_id join, per-question binary/severity_attributes agreement) that motivate a fresh, small pure implementation.
